instruction:
Rotate Middle Arm, Preserve End-Effector World Position

`/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend` contains three mesh objects `Arm1` ← `Arm2` ← `Arm3` in a parent chain, all at zero rotation. Rotate `Arm2` by +30° about its own local Z axis and counter-adjust `Arm3.location` so that `Arm3`'s world-space position is unchanged.

Save the result as `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`.

## Requirements
1. `Arm1`, `Arm2`, `Arm3` all exist as mesh objects in the output.
2. Parent chain is intact: `Arm1` has no parent, `Arm2.parent == Arm1`, `Arm3.parent == Arm2`.
3. `Arm1`'s world transform is unchanged (position ≈ (0,0,0), rotation ≈ (0,0,0); tol 5e-3).
4. `Arm2`'s world position is unchanged (≈ (0, 0.5, 0); tol 5e-3).
5. `Arm2.rotation_euler.z == π/6` (tol 5e-3 rad); its world-frame X/Y rotations remain zero.
6. `Arm3`'s world position matches its original world position (0, 1, 0) to within Euclidean distance 5e-3.
